page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-16 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The hardware configuration allocates 16 GB of system memory, resulting in a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.0 GB per core. This instance does not include bundled local NVMe storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage options.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and cryptographic execution fall within the average range. Specifically, the instance achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 9379.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 22027.2. Memory read bandwidth reaches 1018.3 GB/sec for small cached blocks and drops to 75.4 GB/sec for larger uncached blocks, reflecting standard memory subsystem behavior.

The primary tradeoff of the n2d-highcpu-16 is its highly constrained memory capacity relative to its processing power. With only 1 GB of RAM per vCPU, it is poorly suited for memory-intensive databases or large-scale data processing. However, this resource density provides qualitative cost efficiency for CPU-bound workloads that do not require large memory footprints. It is best suited for tasks such as software compilation, web serving, batch processing, and lightweight text or image processing.
